key_insight: ReLMem learns to compress an evolving patient history into a fixed-size recurrent memory, preserving useful longitudinal information for downstream prediction without rereading all prior visits.
clinical_relevance: This could make long-horizon EHR modeling more computationally practical for tasks like medication prediction while retaining performance close to full-history models.
method: Uses a frozen LLM with lightweight compression adapters to update patient memory visit by visit.
Learns from both intermediate attention alignment between compressed memory and full history and final prediction loss.
Avoids storing or reprocessing the entire record by recurrently updating a fixed-capacity memory.
evidence_signal: On EHR-based medication prediction, ReLMem matched full-history performance closely while cutting retained historical storage by 97.1% and outperforming the strongest compressed-memory baseline by 4.66 macro-F1 and 4.75 micro-F1.
watch_item: Results are reported for a specific EHR prediction setting, so generalization to other clinical tasks, sites, or note types may need additional validation.
paper_title: ReLMem: Learning Recurrent Memory for Longitudinal EHR Modeling
